title: Extra rows from backup history
description: Fix the query so it returns exactly one row per database and exactly two columns: database_name, finished_seq. For a database with successful backups, return the finished_seq of the latest successful backup; a database without a successful backup must remain with finished_seq = NULL. Sort by database_name ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name, b.finished_seq
FROM databases AS d
JOIN backups AS b ON b.database_id = d.id
WHERE b.status = 'success'
ORDER BY d.name;
hints: Reduce multiple successful backups for one database to one value first.
LEFT JOIN preserves databases without successful backups; MAX(finished_seq) chooses the latest sequence.
solution_explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves all databases, while GROUP BY + MAX collapses successful backup history to one row per database.
